editorState:
How to play:

  1. Player 1 draws the main character at the start of the page.
  2. Player 2 thinks of a way to stop the character. It could be anything you like, something small like receiving an invitation to a party, a hole to fall down, or a rocket coming to destroy them. It’s up to you!
  3. Write "1" next to it.
  4. Player 1 thinks of a way to prevent the destruction from happening. Be as creative as you like! Draw it and write "2".
  5. Player 2 thinks of a way of stopping Player 1’s action and draws it.
  6. Keep going until you fill up the page. When there is no more space, go through all your pictures to find out if your character was saved or destroyed!

carouselData.alt: A pencil drawing of a rabbit, with the words "Mr Bunnikins" written above.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Player 1 has drawn a picture of a rabbit and written his name above: "Mr Bunnikins".

carouselData.alt: Next to Mr Bunnikins is a pencil drawing of a carrot, with number "1" written in a circle above it.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Player 2 has drawn a picture of a carrot to distract the rabbit.

carouselData.alt: Next to the carrot is a pan of soup, heating up on a gas hob. There is a number "2" written in a circle above it.
carouselData.labelEditorState: Player 1 has decided to use the carrot to make soup.

carouselData.alt: Next to the pan of soup is a rain cloud with number "3" written in a circle next to it.
carouselData.labelEditorState: But the soup is being rained on! Player 2 has put out the fire which was heating the soup and made the soup all watery.

carouselData.alt: The whole page is now filled with drawings, all the way up to a lake which is labelled with number "25".
carouselData.labelEditorState: The players kept taking it in turns to add drawings until the whole page was filled. But was Mr Bunnikins saved or destroyed?

editorState:
Example game:

Click the arrows to see how the whole game went, and whether Mr Bunnikins was saved or destroyed!

text: A piece of paper with drawings all over - a game of "Saved or Destroyed".

carouselData.alt: Mr Bunnikins
carouselData.labelEditorState: Mr Bunnikins...

carouselData.alt: 1. A carrot.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...was "destroyed" by the carrot (he got distracted and ate it)...

carouselData.alt: 2. A pan of soup on a gas flame.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the soup (the carrot was needed to make the soup)...

carouselData.alt: 3. A rain cloud.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the rain (which put out the fire and diluted the soup)...

carouselData.alt: 4. An umbrella.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the umbrella (which held off the rain)...

carouselData.alt: 5. Wind.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the wind (which blew the umbrella inside-out)...

carouselData.alt: 6. A group of five wind turbines.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the wind farm (which took some energy from the wind)...

carouselData.alt: 7. A close-up view of a wire, with a piece of wood blocking the flow of electricity.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the wooden block (which stopped the electricity)...

carouselData.alt: 8. A lit match.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the match (which burned the wood)...

carouselData.alt: 9. A rectangle representing a swimming pool.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the swimming pool (which put out the match)...

carouselData.alt: 10. A smiling baby in a nappy, which, seems to be leaking.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the baby's nappy leaking (which meant everyone had to get out of the pool)...

carouselData.alt: 11. A toilet.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the toilet (which was a better place for the baby to go)...

carouselData.alt: 12. A roll of loo roll, with the end tangled.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the big ball of loo roll (which blocked the toilet)...

carouselData.alt: 13. A knife with a zigzag blade.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the knife (which cut the loo roll)...

carouselData.alt: 14. A person standing next to a conveyor belt with an x-ray scanner, like the ones you might see at the airport.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the x-ray scanner (which found the knife)...

carouselData.alt: 15. Zigzags of lightning and curved shapes representing thunder noise.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the lightning storm (which destroyed the x-ray machine)...

carouselData.alt: 16. A church with a lightning conductor running down from the top of the steeple.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the lightning conductor on the church (which protected from the lightning)...

carouselData.alt: 17. Lots of circles and lines representing fire.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by fire (which burned down the church)...

carouselData.alt: 18. A fire engine with its ladder up and a hose out.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by a fire engine (which put out the fire)...

carouselData.alt: 19. Two drawing pins, lying with the points facing upwards.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by drawing pins (which burst the tyres of the fire engine)...

carouselData.alt: 20. A horse-shoe shaped magnet.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the magnet (which moved the drawing pins)...

carouselData.alt: 21. A square block of iron.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by the block of iron (which was bigger and more exciting for the magnet)...

carouselData.alt: 22. A stick figure of a Celt. He is wearing trousers, his chest is painted with woad, and he has a wild beard and hair. He is waving a sword.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by the Iron Age person (who needed the iron to make their sword)...

carouselData.alt: 23. A Roman shield and spear.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...destroyed by Romans (who fought the Celts)...

carouselData.alt: 24. A cannon firing a cannon ball.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...saved by a cannon (which could stop Romans)...

carouselData.alt: 25. A curved lake, filling up the rest of the space on the paper.
carouselData.labelEditorState: ...and destroyed by a lake (which the cannon fell into). So in the end, poor Mr Bunnikins didn't make it.

You will need:

  • A piece of paper
  • A pen or pencil to draw with
